requirement:
The harness MUST stop retrying a completion request under
{cite}`requirements.authoring.provider_backoff` when the next attempt would
start more than one minute after the first of its consecutive transient
failures, including when a provider `Retry-After` delay would pass that point.
It MUST then fail the assessment with an error naming the number of attempts
and the last failure's HTTP status and provider error code, when available.
rationale:
I found no test-adequacy gap in the two {test}-marked tests for `requirements.authoring.provider_backoff.limit`. I did not read the implementation. Expected behavior comes from the requirement text.

**Obligations:**
1. Stop retrying when the next attempt would start more than one minute after the first of the consecutive transient failures.
2. Apply that stop even when a `Retry-After` delay would pass the minute.
3. Fail with an error naming the number of attempts and the last failure's HTTP status and provider error code, when available.

**Unit-level coverage:** `src/authoring/providers.rs#mod[tests]/fn[retrying_stops_once_a_request_has_failed_for_a_minute]`
- It drives `ProviderBackoff::retry` with a simulated clock until `Retry::Stop`. It asserts that every `Wait` leaves the next attempt at or before start+60s, and that more than three attempts happen before the stop.
- A second failure at 58s still gets a `Wait` of at most 2s, so retries are not stopped early.
- The `Retry-After` boundary is covered. "60" waits for exactly 60s. "61" stops, so a wait that would start past the minute is refused. "90" stops at once.
- The stop message must contain "kept failing for a minute", "after {attempts+1} attempts" and "HTTP 429 ThrottlingException".
- Partial reports are covered: status only gives "HTTP 503", code only gives "ThrottlingException", and a timeout names its own text. Each case is first retried and then stopped past the limit, which also covers the ten-minute no-response failure.
- A permanent 400 `ValidationException` stops with its own error and without the "kept failing" text.

**Integration-level coverage:** `src/authoring/mod.rs#mod[tests]/fn[a_request_failing_for_a_minute_fails_the_assessment]`
- A provider that always returns 503 `ServiceUnavailableException` runs under paused time through `assess`.
- Elapsed time is at most `RETRY_LIMIT`, and more than three attempts were made.
- The error contains "after {attempts} attempts; last failure: HTTP 503 ServiceUnavailableException", with `attempts` taken from the provider's actual request count.
- The usage log marks the final attempt as `retried: false`.

**Not assessed here:** The reset of the backoff after success is a separate `provider_backoff` obligation. I did not require a test for it here. `success_resets_backoff_and_retries_keep_history_without_repeating_tools` exercises that reset. I could not confirm that test also covers the first-failure clock, because `ProviderBackoff` lives in the external `habeas_sdk`. This is a small residual uncertainty about the "consecutive" wording, not an established gap. The tests do not cover an HTTP-date `Retry-After` past the minute, but the requirement's limit clause makes no distinction by `Retry-After` form.

text: :::{req} provider_backoff.limit
The harness MUST stop retrying a completion request under
{cite}`requirements.authoring.provider_backoff` when the next attempt would
start more than one minute after the first of its consecutive transient
failures, including when a provider `Retry-After` delay would pass that point.
It MUST then fail the assessment with an error naming the number of attempts
and the last failure's HTTP status and provider error code, when available.
:::{req} provider_backoff
When a provider reports a transient failure, the harness MUST wait and retry
the same completion request. Transient failures are throttling, reported
through HTTP 429 or a Bedrock `ThrottlingException`; temporary unavailability,
reported through HTTP 500, 502, 503, or 504 or a Bedrock
`ServiceUnavailableException`, `InternalServerException`, or
`ModelNotReadyException`; and a request with no response after ten minutes,
which the harness MUST abandon. The retry MUST retain its prompt, history,
tools, and pending inputs. It MUST NOT
restart the assessment or repeat already completed tool calls. A permanent
input/context-length error, authentication failure, or invalid request MUST
remain an error; mentioning tokens in an error message alone MUST NOT trigger
retries.
The backoff window MUST start at one second and double after each consecutive
transient failure, up to sixty seconds. Each delay MUST be randomly selected
between half and all of that window to spread parallel retries. An available
provider `Retry-After` value, in seconds or HTTP-date form, MUST be honored as a
minimum delay even when longer than the window. A successful response MUST reset
backoff for the next completion request, and interruption MUST cancel both the
wait and further retries.
Each attempt MUST be recorded under {cite}`requirements.authoring.usage_requests`.
Hidden SDK retries MUST remain disabled so the harness can account for attempts.
Transient retries MUST NOT be reported as finished judgments or terminal
assessment errors while recovery is still in progress. Pending inputs MUST be
recorded as evidence only after the request succeeds.
{cite}`requirements.authoring.provider` {cite}`requirements.authoring.delivered_inputs`
